security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU TCG translates amocas.q (AMOCASQ) gated solely on REQUIRE_ZACAS(ctx) with no ext_ziccamoc CPU flag and no runtime PMA check on the target physical address for coherence and cacheability. The instruction executes on any memory type — RAM, MMIO, or device memory — via tcg_gen_atomic_cmpxchg_i128, which in non-parallel (CF_PARALLEL=0) mode falls through to a fully non-atomic 128-bit load-compare-store sequence (qemu_ld_i128 + XOR-compare + qemu_st_i128) with no PMA gating whatsoever. Similarly, ext_zama16b is checked at translate time to set MO_ATOM_WITHIN16 on load/store memop flags, but QEMU never validates that the target physical address region actually carries the MAG16 PMA — the flag is applied unconditionally to all memory, including regions where MAG16 is not supported.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: REQUIRE_ZACAS without ext_ziccamoc flag or PMA coherence/cacheability check; tcg_gen_atomic_cmpxchg_i128 without PMA gate; ext_zama16b applied to MO_ATOM_WITHIN16 unconditionally without MAG16 PMA validation on target address; missing MULTI_EXT_CFG_BOOL("ziccamoc") in cpu.c; NO PMA coherence/cacheability inspection in atomic_mmu_lookup before any 128-bit atomic path
security_spec.summary: QEMU TCG emulates amocas.q on any memory type without Ziccamoc's coherent+cacheable PMA constraint, and applies Zama16b's MAG16 atomicity guarantee unconditionally without validating the target region's misaligned atomicity granule PMA — a guest kernel assuming RVA23 profile guarantees can trigger non-atomic 128-bit load/store sequences on MMIO/device memory, corrupting device register state
